name: Outdoor ApplianceLinc, firmware 0x42
description: The outdoor on/off module with RF, as firmware 0x42 behaves: its Get Operating Flags reply holds the programming lock, LED on transmit and key beep bits, and it answers Beep. Otherwise it is the Outdoor ApplianceLinc command set.

operatingFlags.name: programmingLock
operatingFlags.label: Programming lock
operatingFlags.description: Linking and programming from the device itself are locked out.

verification.note: Seen on a device running firmware 0x42: after Set Operating Flags with cmd2 0x00, Get Operating Flags (cmd2 0x00) read 0x43; after cmd2 0x01, it read 0x42.

operatingFlags.name: ledOnTransmit
operatingFlags.label: Blink LED when sending
operatingFlags.description: The status LED blinks when the device sends an Insteon message.

verification.note: Seen on a device running firmware 0x42: after Set Operating Flags with cmd2 0x03, Get Operating Flags (cmd2 0x00) read 0x40; after cmd2 0x02, it read 0x42.

operatingFlags.name: keyBeepOff
operatingFlags.label: Key beep off
operatingFlags.description: The key beep setting that Set Operating Flags 0x0B (key beep off) sets and 0x0A (key beep on) clears.

verification.note: Seen on a device running firmware 0x42: after Set Operating Flags with cmd2 0x0A, Get Operating Flags (cmd2 0x00) read 0x02; after cmd2 0x0B, it read 0x42. So the bit is set by 0x0B, which the Outdoor ApplianceLinc with RF Developer Notes give as key beep off, and is 1 when key beep is off. With the bit clear, four taps of the button, each toggling the load, gave no beep, so what the bit changes on the device hasn't been seen.

readings.name: databaseDelta
readings.label: ALL-Link database changes
readings.description: A count that goes up whenever the ALL-Link database changes.

verification.note: Seen on a device running firmware 0x42: Get Operating Flags with an odd cmd2 (0x01, 0x03, 0x05, 0x07 or 0xFF) answered with the ALL-Link database delta, the same value each time, which the cmd1 of the Light Status Request acknowledgment also carried. The device looks only at bit 0 of cmd2: an even cmd2 answers with the operating flags ORed with cmd2. The delta read 0x07 at first; 0x08 after one Read/Write ALL-Link Database write; 0x05 while the device was unlinked, after both of its ALL-Link database records were removed; and 0x08 again after it was linked again and one record rewritten. So it didn't only go up, as the description's count would.

flagCommands.description: Turns Insteon communication over the powerline off. The device turns it back on whenever it powers up.

verification.note: Seen on a device running firmware 0x42: the device acknowledged Set Operating Flags with this cmd2, but no Get Operating Flags reply, with any cmd2, and no byte of the extended Get reply changed with it, so the setting can't be read back.

verification.note: Seen on a device running firmware 0x42: the device acknowledged Beep (cmd1 0x30) and beeped, even when it had no link to the modem that sent it, and also with both of its ALL-Link database records removed and the modem's ALL-Link database empty. The Outdoor ApplianceLinc with RF Developer Notes don't list it.

responder.name: onLevel
responder.label: On-level
responder.description: The on-level; the Outdoor ApplianceLinc with RF Developer Notes say to set it to 0xFE.

responder.name: rampRate
responder.label: Ramp rate
responder.description: The ramp rate; the Outdoor ApplianceLinc with RF Developer Notes say to set it to 0x1F.

verification.note: Seen on a device running firmware 0x42: Light On (cmd1 0x11) with cmd2 0x01 and with cmd2 0x7F turned the load on, and with cmd2 0x00 turned it off; Instant Change (cmd1 0x21) with cmd2 0x01 turned it on, and with cmd2 0x00 turned it off. Light Status Request answered with cmd2 0xFF while the load was on and 0x00 while it was off. No document says that every nonzero level means on; the ranges are read from the status reply's level byte, which read only 0x00 and 0xFF.

notes: The Outdoor ApplianceLinc with RF Developer Notes mark the Get Operating Flags 0x00 reply N/A. Seen on a device running firmware 0x42: it answered, and the device looks only at bit 0 of cmd2. An odd cmd2 answers with the ALL-Link database delta. An even cmd2 answers with the operating flags ORed with cmd2: with the flags at 0x42, cmd2 0x00 and 0x02 read 0x42, 0x04 read 0x46, 0x08 read 0x4A, 0x10 read 0x52, 0x20 read 0x62 and 0x80 read 0xC2. So query with cmd2 0x00 for the flags and 0x01 for the delta.
Seen on a device running firmware 0x42: bits 2 to 5 and bit 7 of the flags always read 0.

Seen on a device running firmware 0x42: before any change, the flags read 0x42: programming lock off, LED on transmit on and key beep off. The device was secondhand, so these may not be its factory settings, and the catalog gives no defaults.

It sends Set Operating Flags as extended messages with a checksum in D14. Seen on a device running firmware 0x42: X10 (0x12, 0x13), error blink (0x14, 0x15) and cleanup report (0x16, 0x17) were acknowledged, but no Get Operating Flags reply and no byte of the extended Get reply changed with them, so they stay flag commands with no bit.

Seen on a device running firmware 0x42: the extended Get reply's data read 0x01 0x01 0x0F 0xEF 0x00 0x00 0x1C 0xFE 0x20 0x00 0x00 0x01 0x26 0xD1, and no flag change altered it. D12 and D13 changed between some reads with no flag change: later reads gave 0x02 0x4B, then 0x02 0x65, then 0x02 0x6F. They stayed the same across reads while the device was idle and only went up, and one on/off cycle of the load raised them by 10, so they look like they count the device's activity. D3 and D4 (0x0F 0xEF), D9 (0x20) and D12 and D13 aren't explained by any document.
The Outdoor ApplianceLinc with RF Developer Notes give no extended Set for the settings its Get reports.

The Outdoor ApplianceLinc with RF Developer Notes say the device sends its Assign to ALL-Link Group broadcast on power-up and supports only responder links, whose on-level should be 0xFE and ramp rate 0x1F. Seen on a device running firmware 0x42: holding its SET button made it the controller of group 1, but tapping the button sent no group commands over that link. After 10 seconds without power, the load, which had been on, came back on, and no message from the device reached the modem in the 15 seconds after it was plugged back in.

Seen on a device running firmware 0x42: with both of its ALL-Link database records removed and the modem's ALL-Link database empty, the device acknowledged Light Status Request, with cmd1 0x05 and cmd2 0xFF while the load was on. It answered Get Insteon Engine Version (cmd1 0x0D), Get Operating Flags (cmd1 0x1F, cmd2 0x00) and Ping with a NAK carrying cmd2 0xFF, and didn't answer ID Request. While unlinked, it also rejected Light On (cmd1 0x11) with a NAK carrying cmd2 0xFF. The operating flags (0x42), ramp rate (0x1C) and on-level (0xFE) read the same after it was unlinked and linked again.

Seen on a device running firmware 0x42: the device writes its own responder record when it's linked remotely, with Start ALL-Linking on the modem and Enter Linking Mode sent to the device, and sets Data 1 from the load's state at the time of the link: 0x00 when the load was off and 0xFF when it was on, never the 0xFE above. Linked as responder to a Hub 2245's group 0 while its load was off, its record held Data 1 to 3 as 0x00 0x1F 0x00; turned on with Light On (cmd1 0x11) first and linked again, 0xFF 0x1F 0x00. Data 2 was 0x1F, the ramp rate, on these links and 0x00 on an earlier one, whose record held 0xFF 0x00 0x00; a link made over that record later gave 0x00 0x00 0x00, and with on-level 0x00 an On to group 0 from the modem left the load off. With Data 1 0xFF, an On to group 0 from the modem turned the load on and an Off turned it off. Its controller record for group 1, to the Hub, held 0x03 0x00 0x00. Read/Write ALL-Link Database (cmd1 0x2F) with D2 0x02, writing that record with Data 0xFE 0x1F 0x00, was acknowledged and read back as written; then an On to group 0 from the modem turned the load on and an Off turned it off.

The Outdoor ApplianceLinc with RF Developer Notes give the device's identity as category 0x01 and subcategory 0x3A, which the catalog gives to the 2672 LED bulb; the catalog keeps 0x02 and 0x38 for the 2634-222.
